So which is it? Under sea cables or satellites?

For every home network, the advertisement promises blazing wireless bandwidth (currently up to ~1 Gbit/s shared between all devices).

However, what they don't tell you is that for cables (Ethernet), dedicated (per device) 1Gbit/s bandwidth was reliably available 15 years ago. Today you can have 10 Gbit/s Ethernet bandwidth for a reasonable price.

The same is true for satellites. You can have blazing maximum bandwidths of 140 Gbit/s for a 2011 satellite (ViaSat-1) but for a single 2001 transatlantic cable (TAT-14), we are using 3.15 Tbit/s out of 9.38 Tbit/s maximum bandwidth.

1 x TAT-14 cable = 67 x ViaSat-1 satellites

So today's traffic definitely is more important in cable than satellites.

As for the 20 000 satellites for 5G, those are still in planning to be put in service by SpaceX. Note that 5G does not require satellites but it's just one of the options.
